title: Nothing Clears the Ceiling
gallery_text: With the grant set to zero, not one of the 22,333 eligible lots in Queens can be financed - every single one costs more to build than the programme will lend. The ceiling and the cost come from two different HPD documents and nobody reconciled them.
description:
One value is changed from the published terms: the grant is zero. That is the version of the programme that exists if nobody funds it.

At the real grant of $175,000, 14,883 of 22,333 eligible lots clear the cushion. At zero, none do - and they fail for a reason worth separating out. They do not fail on cash flow. They fail on the $220,000 loan ceiling, before rent is ever considered. The median eligible lot takes a 333 square foot unit, which costs $201,000 to build at HPD's own median published figure of $603 a square foot, plus $146,480 of soft cost by HPD's own budgeting formula. That is $347,480 against a ceiling of $220,000. The gap is $127,480, and the grant is what closes it.

Even with the grant, 31.5% of eligible lots still exceed the ceiling. The three numbers - the $220,000 cap, the $175,000 grant, and the $603 - come from three separate HPD publications: a term sheet, a term sheet, and a plan library. Nothing in any of them refers to the others.
